clue.text: Scorn trick bait

parts.note: to con someone is to trick or swindle them
to bait is to tempt or lure

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a cheap trick used as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name disdain felt towards something judged worthless; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Cads are possibly without: aspiration to organise parlour games

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
possibly says the letters of the preceding words may be rearranged

parts.note: H stands for aspiration, the breathed sound in phonetics

explanation.surface: Uncouth men wishing to set up some party games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CADS ARE, which goes 'without' (outside) H.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party guessing game acted in mime, played in drawing rooms.

clue.text: The dark horse can make one's hair stand on end!

definitions.text: can make one's hair stand on end

parts.note: night is the dark time
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: An unknown racing contender can be terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark horse' is an idiom for an unknown contender, a false lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream that terrifies.

clue.text: Ways foreign money may be acquired in Germany

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are two compass directions or ways
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: How a traveller might obtain currency while in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Charge after a mount for example

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar

indicators.note: in a down clue mount means climbing upward, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A fee payable after a horse, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee for sending mail.

clue.text: Arranges about parking for games

indicators.note: about here means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to sort things is to arrange them
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone organises the car park ahead of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports are athletic contests, which is what games means in the plural school or Olympic sense.

clue.text: Deficient in pep and pale, fruit's called for

indicators.note: deficient suggests something defective, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lacking energy and pallid, someone needs fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a tropical fruit with spiky skin.

clue.text: A dictator made to measure!

explanation.surface: A tyrant who fits his role perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is one who governs, and also a straight measuring strip.

clue.text: Their voices were seductive in the main

definitions.text: Their voices were seductive in the main

parts.words: Their voices were seductive in the main
parts.note: main is the sea: mythical singers who lured sailors

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the singing sea-nymphs lured sailors onto rocks.

clue.text: Value credit-entry in the depression

indicators.note: entry means going in, so the value enters the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to rate is to value

explanation.surface: Accounting entries during an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a hollow, a dip in the ground.

clue.text: The butterfly has, of course, multiple eyes

explanation.surface: A butterfly is noted for the many eye-spots on its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the mythical giant, whose many eyes are a matter of course for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus is a butterfly with eye-like wing spots, and in Greek myth the giant guardian with a hundred eyes.

clue.text: Trainee has foreigner in splits — he's killing!

indicators.note: the trainee splits the foreigner, so one piece is broken open by the other

parts.note: a stranger is an outsider or foreigner
L for learner, the plate a trainee driver displays

explanation.surface: A newcomer laughs so hard at a foreign visitor that it is killing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a murderer who chokes victims, so he is a man in the act of killing.

clue.text: Servant, a sober worker, receives a tip

indicators.note: receives means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. sober
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
a tip is an end, as in the tip of a finger

explanation.surface: A teetotal employee is handed a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant is someone who waits on others, a helper in service.

clue.text: .The front cover

explanation.surface: A front cover, as of a book or magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is the forward part of a theatre stage, and also a garment worn to protect clothing.

clue.text: A model at one time stout

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so it stands for at one time
ample means large or well-filled, like stout

explanation.surface: A fashion model who was once rather plump.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern to be copied, which is what a model is.

clue.text: A course set at intervals?

parts.note: a meal course served bit by bit, in pieces

explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, piece by piece.

clue.text: Ring again to make a cancellation

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to peal is to ring, as church bells do

explanation.surface: Someone phones a second time to cancel a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: Give faint indication of a silent, tear maybe

parts.note: dumb means without speech, silent

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of tear may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A single silent teardrop hints at sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to outline or foreshadow vaguely.

clue.text: With a little love, get a tearaway to live a quiet life

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: With some affection, a wild youth may settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: To vegetate is to lead a dull, inactive existence.

clue.text: Leave the proper payment.

explanation.surface: Someone walks away from the fee they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon; one's desert, as in just deserts, is what one rightly deserves.

clue.text: Nae man can _____ time or tide" (Burns)

definitions.text: Nae man can _____ time or tide" (Burns)

parts.words: Nae man can _____ time or tide" (Burns)
parts.note: a line from Robert Burns's Tam o' Shanter with one word to supply

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from the Scottish poet Robert Burns; nae is Scots for no.
explanation.definitionFit: Burns wrote that no man can tie up or restrain time or tide.

clue.text: Believe the composition supreme

indicators.note: composition means putting together anew, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the musical work is outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to suppose or take as true without proof.

clue.text: Painter's equipment the head allowed inside

indicators.note: inside signals one piece put within the other

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An artist's gear kept inside the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the board an artist mixes colours on.

clue.text: Alarm caused by misdoing after the start of term

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes behind the first
the start of takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an error is a misdoing or mistake

explanation.surface: Panic from wrongdoing early in the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, a stronger alarm.

clue.text: English backing Ireland? That would be strange!

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for Ireland is read in reverse

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An Englishman supporting Ireland would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns EIRE into ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird or uncanny, a synonym for odd.

clue.text: Sally keeps quiet when flying

indicators.note: keeps means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sally is a sortie or raid
P is piano, the musical term for quiet

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally stays silent on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means very fast, as in a flying visit.

clue.text: It's only fair the board should accept new role

indicators.note: accept means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

indicators.note: new signals the letters of role are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The company board fairly takes on a fresh role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes OLER from ROLE, which goes inside TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means passable or acceptable, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: The crest of a bird with a bit missing

indicators.note: missing says a piece is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the partridge is a game bird
a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: A bird's crest with a piece absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The crest looks like a feather tuft, but it is a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised crest of land.

clue.text: Theatre company object to act

parts.note: rep is short for repertory, a theatre company
to resent something is to take objection to it

explanation.surface: A drama troupe refuses to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent someone is to act on their behalf.

clue.text: A little drink before a show

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A quick tot before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a theatrical production.

clue.text: Courteously converse

parts.note: converse is a noun here: the opposite of politely, not talking politely

explanation.definitionFit: Rudely is the opposite of politely, in a discourteous manner.

clue.text: Low-down woman — south-east- European citizen

parts.note: gen is slang for information, the low-down
Eve, the first woman
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A base woman from the south-east of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Genevese is a native of Geneva, a Swiss city.
